title: Anthropic’s Rust API: what the tests said, and what real traffic showed
intro: Switch between April 2026, when the new Rust version had passed nearly all its tests, and the finished move, to see why Anthropic checked the new API against real requests before switching over.
note: All figures are Anthropic’s own, from its engineering post of 25 November 2026, and most are approximate (“about”). The April match rate compares the Rust and Python versions on live production requests, step by step; the tests are Anthropic’s existing set of about 700 integration tests. The CPU figure is for one region, and the time-to-first-token figure is for customers’ Claude Code requests over a shorter period. Nothing here was measured independently.
